exploitation_prerequisites:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.
rationale: Present in the exact image and linked by optional libpq-oauth-18.so. Standard postgres/libpq direct ldd output alone does not rule out dynamically loaded OAuth reachability. Brotli requires a crafted compressed response; curl requires an HTTP/2 upload and malicious RST_STREAM. Florabase normal SCRAM connections do not configure OAuth; client tools/extensions/operator actions can activate additional paths, which runtime policy has not independently excluded. Prefer a separately reviewed PostgreSQL maintenance image with fixed libraries, not a vulnerability waiver.

exploitation_prerequisites:

(with reason `HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED` or `REFUSED_STREAM`) leading to a use after
free of a `struct Curl_easy` object.

exploitation_prerequisites: During session resumption in crypto/tls, if the underlying Config has its ClientCAs or RootCAs fields mutated between the initial handshake and the resumed handshake, the resumed handshake may succeed when it should have failed. This may happen when a user calls Config.Clone and mutates the returned Config, or uses Config.GetConfigForClient. This can cause a client to resume a session with a server that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake, or cause a server to resume a session with a client that it would not have resumed with during the initial handshake.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: The net/url package does not set a limit on the number of query parameters in a query. While the maximum size of query parameters in URLs is generally limited by the maximum request header size, the net/http.Request.ParseForm method can parse large URL-encoded forms. Parsing a large form containing many unique query parameters can cause excessive memory consumption.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Within HostnameError.Error(), when constructing an error string, there is no limit to the number of hosts that will be printed out. Furthermore, the error string is constructed by repeated string concatenation, leading to quadratic runtime. Therefore, a certificate provided by a malicious actor can result in excessive resource consumption.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: On most platforms, Go uses the given system root certificates. However, in some narrower cases, the system trust stores may not be updated without further action. To defend against the narrower set of cases that may remain affected, a denylist was added in crypto/x509 to return an error when calling Verify with any of the known intermediate certificates that are no longer considered to be trustworthy.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: url.Parse insufficiently validated the host/authority component and accepted some invalid URLs.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: (*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: During chain building, the amount of work that is done is not correctly limited when a large number of intermediate certificates are passed in VerifyOptions.Intermediates, which can lead to a denial of service. This affects both direct users of crypto/x509 and users of crypto/tls.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Validating certificate chains which use policies is unexpectedly inefficient when certificates in the chain contain a very large number of policy mappings, possibly causing denial of service. This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Well-crafted inputs reaching ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate were able to trigger excessive CPU exhaustion and memory allocations.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: The ToASCII and ToUnicode functions incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only label. For example, ToUnicode("xn--example-.com") incorrectly returns the name "example.com" rather than an error. This behavior can lead to privilege escalation in programs using the idna package. For example, a program which performs privilege checks on the ASCII hostname may reject "example.com" but permit "xn--example-.com". If that program subsequently converts the ASCII hostname to Unicode, it will inadvertently permits access to the Unicode name "example.com".
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: On Unix systems, opening a file in an os.Root improperly follows symlinks to locations outside of the Root when the final path component of the a path is a symbolic link and the path ends in /. For example, 'root.Open("symlink/")' will open "symlink" even when "symlink" is a symbolic link pointing outside of the root.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: The Dial and LookupPort functions panic on Windows when provided with an input containing a NUL (0).
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Decoding a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words can consume excessive CPU.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads a few bytes from each new connection to see if they contain the HTTP/2 client preface. ReadHeaderTimeout is unexpectedly not being applied when doing this.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Previously, pathological inputs could close an unescaped '/' early, allowing for attack-controlled data to inject arbitrary content, potentially leading to XSS.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Previously, DecodeElement would reset the depth counter causing it to never fire; this could lead to stack exhaustion.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Previously, resolving relative paths containing parent directory ('..') segments performed string conversions and buffer rewrites on each step, resulting in quadratic time complexity and high memory allocation overhead. Now, path resolution operates on a byte buffer using index-based backtracking for '..' segments, eliminating the quadratic time complexity and significantly reducing memory allocations.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Handshake messages, such as KeyUpdate, are always considered as state-advancing, regardless of whether a handshake has been completed or not. As a result, a malicious client can keep sending KeyUpdate messages to force the server to keep performing key derivation operations indefinitely.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: When parsing a Range header containing a large number of small ranges, FileServer(FS), ServeContent, and ServeFile(FS) can consume an excessive amount of CPU.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption in the client or server by opening a large number of streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.

exploitation_prerequisites: Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in the server process by specifying multiple references. We now reject these as malformed and curb the memory amplification vector as a result.
rationale_reference: Shared source/binary assessment in docs/beta-security-001.md and postgresql-runtime-inspection.json; advisory prerequisite retained per entry.
